_comment: Provenance for WASM bundles built from the pqctoday-hsm repo and vendored into this hub. When you rebuild a bundle with its hsm build script, update its `hsmCommit`/`builtAt`. Verify drift with `npm run sync:wasm:check` (compares against a sibling ../pqctoday-hsm checkout when present; no-op otherwise). Bundles built from other sources (openssl upstream, pqctoday-tpm) are intentionally omitted.

bundles.name: cacp-kmip
bundles._buildNote: Rebuilt 2026-08-09 from hsm main @ 1cab535 via scripts/build-kmip-wasm.sh. This is the one bundle of the three with a REAL input change: kmip/src/server/listener.rs gained 42 lines between 3480bec2d and 1cab535 (TlsProfile::ClassicalBaseline on server and client — the same-provider baseline that makes the quantum-safe comparison honest, since permissive-vs-quantum-safe also varies the crypto provider). Verified by the build's own smoke suite running IN wasm, not by exit code: OASIS Query → Success, Create symmetric key → real keygen, malformed frame → error response with no exception, CreateKeyPair/Sign/SignatureVerify ML-DSA-65 round trip (3309-byte signature, Valid), Falcon-512 correctly rejected with the keystore unchanged, and an X25519MLKEM768 hybrid KEM CreateKeyPair→Activate→Encapsulate→Decapsulate round trip. 144 corpus tests staged.

bundles.name: softhsmrustv3-engine
bundles._buildNote: Re-anchored 2026-08-09 to hsm main @ 1cab535. REBUILT AND PROVEN IDENTICAL rather than re-anchored on assertion: running rust/build-wasm-bundle.sh at 1cab535 produced softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, softhsmrustv3_bg.js, softhsmrustv3.js and both .d.ts files BYTE-IDENTICAL to the ones already shipped (wasm sha256 310d3a91…), so no file in the hub changed — only this pin. The source diff predicts exactly that: between the previously recorded 3e2f5055b and 1cab535, the only change anywhere under rust/ is rust/bench-harness/src/kmip.rs, which no bundle builds from. Export surface unchanged at 91 distinct C_* symbols (same set), and the binary contains zero bench-harness symbols. NOTE FOR THE NEXT READER: this bundle's sourceDirs is ['rust'], which CONTAINS rust/bench-harness, so the drift gate counts bench commits as inputs and will keep reporting false drift here. Rebuilding on that signal is how bench code would get baked into shipped wasm — check the diff excludes rust/bench-harness before believing a stale report. RE-ANCHORED to dc9c0a838 (same day, minutes later): committing the rebuilt artifact back to hsm is ITSELF a commit under rust/, so the gate immediately reported 1 commit of fresh drift against a bundle that had just been proven current — the tail-chase the 2026-08-08 note on this file already described. dc9c0a838 changes exactly one file, rust/pkg_bundler/softhsmrustv3_bg.wasm, which is the tracked build OUTPUT the hub vendors, not a source input. Verified rather than asserted: the wasm shipped here and the blob inside dc9c0a838 have the same sha256 (310d3a91…), so this pin names the commit that literally CONTAINS the bytes being shipped. This will recur every time an artifact is committed back to hsm while these bundles keep 'rust' in sourceDirs.

Those two commits are the apply_mldsa_patches.py anchor fix and its --dry-run preflight; the build still pins OPENSSH_VERSION=V_10_3_P1, and on 10.3 there are no upstream-inserted key types for the widened anchor to preserve, so the patched source is unchanged. openssh-server.js came out byte-identical; only openssh-server.wasm moved, because it statically links the freshly rebuilt libsofthsmv3-static.a. bundles.name: openssl-pkcs11
bundles._rebuild20260807: Rebuilt 2026-08-07 from hsm main @ 67f739f (merge of PR #153, feat/rust-pkcs11-emscripten-staticlib), closing a 3-commit drift — the same feature branch this bundle's _priorBuild/_buildNote below already describe now landed on main via a clean merge (hsm main's rust/ tree after the merge is identical to 859774b's, confirmed via `git log --stat`). NOTE: the hsmCommit given in the original task request (67f739fc3916b08fe59445120d93f26dfd79d639) does not exist in the hsm repo — corrected here to the actual merge-commit HEAD (67f739fc331cfdb1406197583cf6432f52833080), verified via `git rev-parse HEAD` in pqctoday-hsm. Rebuilt fresh end-to-end per the established process: scripts/build-pkcs11-provider-wasm.sh prerequisite (idempotent — archive already current), a fresh wasm32-unknown-emscripten Rust staticlib build with --features acvp (superseding the stale 2026-07-24 archive), OpenSSL 3.6.3 source re-verified against the pinned sha256 (243a86649cf6f23eeb6a2ff2456e09e5d77dd9018a54d3d96b0c6bdd6ba6c7f1) before extracting, then pqctoday-priv/build-wasm.sh with HUB_ROOT/HSM_ROOT/OPENSSL_SRC set explicitly. Since the underlying rust/ tree is unchanged from the last build, the resulting binary is FUNCTIONALLY IDENTICAL to the previous one — this rebuild is provenance/timestamp hygiene, not a behavior change. VERIFIED: `openssl version` reports 3.6.3; all custom exports present (_pqctoday_cms_init, _pqctoday_composite_mkcert, _execute_cmp_simulation, PKCS#11 C_* symbols); 17/17 real ML-DSA/SLH-DSA/ML-KEM cross-implementation KATs (Node 24 crypto vs this WASM binary) pass; 72/72 in the rest of the OpenSSL Studio + anchor-KAT suites (89 total, 0 failed); `npx tsc -b` clean.
bundles._rebuild20260802: Rebuilt 2026-08-02 from hsm main @ 8386717 (v0.20.2), closing a 6-commit drift AND moving the bundled OpenSSL from 3.6.2 to 3.6.3 (deliberate, user-approved — hsm's deps/openssl-wasm had already moved to 3.6.3 in v0.19.0, so the bundle was behind on both axes). Source: openssl-3.6.3.tar.gz from the official GitHub release, sha256 verified against the published checksum (243a86649cf6f23eeb6a2ff2456e09e5d77dd9018a54d3d96b0c6bdd6ba6c7f1) before extracting. Build needs a prerequisite the main script does not build itself: scripts/build-pkcs11-provider-wasm.sh must run first to produce build-wasm/lib/libpkcs11-provider.a, otherwise build-wasm.sh exits immediately with 'missing pkcs11-provider archive'. Invoked as: HUB_ROOT=<hub checkout> HSM_ROOT=<hsm> OPENSSL_SRC=<openssl-3.6.3 tree> bash pqctoday-priv/build-wasm.sh (HUB_ROOT must be set explicitly — the script's location-derived default is wrong since it moved into pqctoday-priv). The 'apps/openssl link failed (undefined symbol: pqctoday_cms_init)' line in the log is EXPECTED and handled — the script continues to its own custom emcc link; do not read it as a build failure. VERIFIED: `openssl version` now reports 3.6.3 (via the real driver harness, not assumed); OpenSSL Studio suites 57/57 main + 32/32 local incl. the ML-DSA/ML-KEM cross-implementation and anchor KATs, all of which re-confirm real crypto outputs against this new binary; and — closing the prior entry's explicit 'NOT YET VERIFIED: a full pass in an actual browser' gap — e2e/cms-hsm-sign.spec.ts 5/5 in real chromium, including T3 routing an ML-DSA-65 CMS signature through pkcs11-provider into softhsmv3 with 'HSM (pkcs11:)' / 'resident in softhsmv3' evidence. Version references across the Studio's UI copy, lessons, glossary and KAT comments were updated 3.6.2 -> 3.6.3; the only 3.6.2 mentions left are dated historical records of when content was first captured. STILL UNCONFIRMED (carried over): whether the 'HRR detection' patch referenced by the build script's banner is present in this tree.
